decision.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 6 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 6 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed lowered borrowing costs by 50 basis points to 6 percent to support economic growth.

changes.quote: In a related action, the Board of Governors approved a 25-basis-point decrease in the discount rate to 5-3/4 percent, the level requested by seven Reserve Banks.
changes.explanation: The Board also lowered the discount rate charged on direct bank loans by 25 basis points to 5-3/4 percent.

changes.quote: These actions were taken in light of further weakening of sales and production, and in the context of lower consumer confidence, tight conditions in some segments of financial markets, and high energy prices sapping household and business purchasing power.
changes.explanation: The Fed pointed to softening sales, lower confidence, tight financial conditions, and high energy prices as reasons for the rate cut.
The central bank noted that inflation is not currently a major concern.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 6 percent.

These actions were taken in light of further weakening of sales and production, and in the context of lower consumer confidence, tight conditions in some segments of financial markets, and high energy prices sapping household and business purchasing power.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.98% APR, a 50 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 5.14% and moved +22 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.17% would rise by about $44.82 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 3.9%, and employers added an average of 107k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.4% over the past year (November 2000); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 0.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve is closely watching weakening sales and production to determine if further rate cuts are needed. Upcoming meetings will likely evaluate incoming economic data to see if additional easing is warranted.
